An '''aperiodic finite-state automaton''' (also called a '''counter-free automaton''') is a [[finite-state automaton]] whose [[transition monoid]] is [[aperiodic monoid|aperiodic]].

== Definition ==
A finite-state automaton  is '''counter-free''' if the following property is true:

* as long as there is a loop in the automaton that can be taken with a word <math>u^m</math> (i.e. word <math>u</math> repeated <math>m</math> times) for <math>m \geq 1</math> from state <math>q</math> to state  <math>q</math>, then we also go from <math>q</math> to <math>q</math> by reading word <math>u</math>.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Diekert |first=Volker |last2=Gastin |first2=Paul |title=First-order definable languages. |url=https://www2.informatik.uni-stuttgart.de/fmi/ti/veroeffentlichungen/pdffiles/DiekertGastin2008SIWT.pdf}}</ref>{{page needed|reason=I didn't find the definition in the paper.|date=August 2026}}

==Properties==
A [[regular language]] is [[Star-free language|star-free]] if and only if it is accepted by an automaton with a finite and aperiodic [[transition monoid]]. This result of algebraic [[automata theory]] is due to [[Marcel-Paul Schützenberger]].<ref name="Schutzenberger65">{{cite journal| author=Schützenberger, Marcel-Paul| title=On Finite Monoids Having Only Trivial Subgroups| journal=[[Information and Control]]| year=1965| volume=8| number=2| pages=190–194| url=http://igm.univ-mlv.fr/~berstel/Mps/Travaux/A/1965-4TrivialSubgroupsIC.pdf| doi=10.1016/s0019-9958(65)90108-7| doi-access=free}}</ref>
In particular, the [[DFA minimization|minimum automaton]] of a star-free language is always counter-free (however, a star-free language may also be recognized by other automata that are not aperiodic).

A '''counter-free language''' is a regular language for which there is an integer ''n'' such that for all words ''x'', ''y'', ''z'' and integers ''m'' ≥ ''n'' we have ''xy''<sup>''m''</sup>''z'' in ''L'' if and only if ''xy''<sup>''n''</sup>''z'' in ''L''. For these languages, when a string contains enough repetitions of any [[substring]] (at least ''n'' repetitions), changing the number of repetitions to another number that is at least ''n'' cannot change membership in the language. (This is automatically true when ''y'' is the [[empty string]], but becomes a nontrivial condition when ''y'' is non-empty.) Another way to state Schützenberger's theorem is that star-free languages and counter-free languages are the same thing.

An aperiodic automaton satisfies the [[Černý conjecture]].<ref name="Trahtman07">{{cite journal | zbl=1152.68461 | last=Trahtman | first=Avraham N. | authorlink=Avraham Trahtman | title=The Černý conjecture for aperiodic automata | journal=[[Discrete Math. Theor. Comput. Sci.]] | volume=9 | number=2 | pages=3–10 | year=2007 | issn=1365-8050 | url=http://www.dmtcs.org/dmtcs-ojs/index.php/dmtcs/article/downloadSuppFile/649/30 | access-date=2014-04-05 | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150923215445/http://www.dmtcs.org/dmtcs-ojs/index.php/dmtcs/article/downloadSuppFile/649/30 | archive-date=2015-09-23 | url-status=dead }}</ref>
